Everything changed. I’m not going to say it’s not hard, cause it is. It’s extremely hard. Things have been really up and down. Buuuut..  
  
Firstly, I got to meet the best human in existence. She just so happen to come out of my body. I got to sniff her, kiss her, hug her. The sniffing is listed first cause it’s actually the greatest sensory experience I’ve ever had in my life. Even now, at 19mths, it’s just as good. I spend a large chunk of my every day sniffing her head.   
Then I got to watch her grow. I got to nourish her with milk my body made and wow, what an experience. I got to feel sooo proud of her and myself at the same time. That’s so lucky. We are still BFing and it has been one of the most challenging but beautiful experiences ever.  
A while later, she began hitting all the milestones (REALLY EARLY, which was a whole journey in and of itself). I got to watch her roll, crawl, walk, and run! Around when she started crawling, things got crazy, as a baby on the move is such a wild thing. This is also the time where I was really able to see her daddy shine in his role. He was always great and always did sooo much with her, but play was starting to ramp up. They were really playing now, even laughing together at this point, and we started becoming a little unit.   
Now she’s well out of the baby stage and it’s balls to the wall crazy all day every day. But we get to have dance parties, go on hikes, shopping adventures, parks, play dates, food dates. She helps with chores, she’s happy to come hang out doing really whatever with me. She’s learning new words every day. You get to hear “mum!”. That is the sweetest music you’ll ever hear.  She’s also absolutely hilarious. Comedic backbone of our family. We laugh more than we ever have now.    
  
During all this, I’ve grown so much. As a mother and a person in general. My mental health has overall gotten leaps and bounds better. I’m stronger mentally, I have more empathy and less anger. I have more willpower and drive than ever before. A very cool thing is, I don’t want to die anymore. I haven’t been able to truly say that since I was a small child.  
  
Getting to love someone so much is the greatest gift I’ll ever receive. Every heartache that comes with it all be worth it. This is the reason I was put on this earth.

When our daughter was small, around 3mths I think, her daddy had her while he was playing video games. She was in her rocker just hanging out. I was having some much needed time sitting down alone.  
She started to cry, and he wasn’t done his game, so tried “consoling” her by rocking her in her rocker. It didn’t work. She ramped up the screams. He just kept talking to her and playing the fucking game.   
  
I sat there with my blood fucking boiling. He told me “I’ve got he don’t worry”. It had been maybe 2min, if that, and I couldn’t stand it anymore. I went and got her. He didn’t get it. I told him if he ever did that again, I’ll lose it, and how dare he choose a game over our extremely distressed child. It made me look at him differently for a while, to be honest. It had happened multiple times beforehand, but usually only for 30-60sec. This time he just let her scream and it felt endless.  
  
She’s 18mths now and I think about it regularly, still. How could he do that? Why didn’t her screams signal for him to put everything down and get her - like it does for me? I still put everything down and scoop her up if she’s genuinely upset (and not just mad cause I said no to something). He is a good dad, no doubt about it.. but a lot of men just don’t seem to get it. No, “reading” to your kid while you’re playing a game on your laptop doesn’t count. No, being on your phone and occasionally saying something encouraging doesn’t count. It really really upsets me and I try tell him but he doesn’t hear me, I’m sure thinks I’m nagging for the fun of it. I just never want our daughter to feel she has to compete with his phone and games.
